card.text: Earth's only natural satellite, always turning the same face toward us.

introduction.text: The Moon likely formed after a Mars-sized body collided with Earth. Its dark maria are old impact basins filled with lava.

surface.title: LROC photographic mosaic
surface.summary: LRO photographs from 2009–2011; crater shadows are part of the images.

midnight-temperature.title: LRO Diviner GHRM: midnight temperature
midnight-temperature.summary: Midnight temperatures fitted from Diviner data, 2009–2022, within 70° of the equator. They average many nights.

heat-anomalies.title: LRO Diviner GHRM: heat anomalies
heat-anomalies.summary: Midnight warmth (red) or coolness (blue) compared with typical lunar soil. Warm spots are not signs of internal heat.

rock-abundance.title: LRO Diviner GHRM: rock abundance
rock-abundance.summary: The share of ground covered by rocks, modeled from Diviner midnight data. It estimates area, not boulder counts.

topography.title: LOLA LDEM16 elevation model
topography.summary: Height above or below a 1,737.4 km sphere, from LRO's laser altimeter. Shading shows slopes.

crust.title: Crustal-thickness model
crust.summary: Thickness inferred from gravity and topography. It depends on assumed rock densities.

gravity.title: GRAIL gravity anomaly (GRGM1200A)
gravity.summary: Where the Moon pulls harder (red) or softer (blue) than a smooth, even sphere, measured by the twin GRAIL probes in 2012.

bouguer-gravity.title: GRAIL Bouguer gravity (GRGM1200A)
bouguer-gravity.summary: Gravity with the pull of hills and craters removed, so what remains comes from denser or lighter rock underground.

silicate-signature.title: Diviner Christiansen feature, 2009–2016
silicate-signature.summary: An infrared emissivity peak between 8.0 and 8.5 µm that tracks silicate composition, not mineral amounts.

geology.title: USGS unified global geology (2020 v2)
geology.summary: Geologic units and their relative ages from the 2020 USGS map. Colors are map units, not surface color.

submicroscopic-iron.title: Iron particles from space weathering
submicroscopic-iron.summary: Tiny metallic iron particles build up as space exposure alters lunar soil; the model estimates their amount.

plagioclase-grain-size.title: Fine or coarse plagioclase grains
plagioclase-grain-size.summary: Plagioclase is a mineral in highland rocks; the model tries fine or coarse grains to match the reflected light.

plagioclase.title: Mineral in the bright highlands
plagioclase.summary: Plagioclase is a mineral common in the Moon’s bright highland rocks; colors estimate its share of the surface material.

iron-oxide.title: Iron estimated from reflected light
iron-oxide.summary: Iron in the surface material, reported as iron oxide (FeO); colors show the estimated percentage by weight.

olivine.title: Olivine in surface rocks
olivine.summary: Olivine is a mineral made with iron and magnesium, found in volcanic rocks; colors estimate its share by weight.

orthopyroxene.title: Low-calcium pyroxene
orthopyroxene.summary: Orthopyroxene is a rock-forming mineral with little calcium; its distribution helps distinguish lunar rock mixtures.

clinopyroxene.title: High-calcium pyroxene
clinopyroxene.summary: This map estimates calcium-rich pyroxene, a mineral found in volcanic rocks; colors show its share by weight.

optical-maturity.title: Changes from exposure to space
optical-maturity.summary: Sunlight reflected by the soil reveals changes from exposure to space; lower values indicate more weathered material.
